scope_quality_evidence.context:
P9.7 content criteria are not applicable as a copy judgment: this change modifies no governed page or content source.
Authoritative requirements from docs/plan/MASTER_PLAN.md (read from the candidate; plan hash remains governed by plan:check):
| P9.7 | Content quality gate (R-CONT-01..05, Google quality bar). Every blog post and content page meets: (a) canonical formatting — shared inline style block byte-identical across posts, uniform headers/footers/CTA structure, metadata/JSON-LD parity, H1/title alignment; (b) SEO — real search demand, unique intent per URL, sitemap + structured data valid, no cannibalization; (c) sourcing — verifiable claims with cited sources, official sources only for news hooks; (d) voice — R-CONT-01..04 (plain, second person, ≤ grade 8 reading level, no hype/fear/sales language). Jev judges content PRs against this bar at ≥ 99 with full confidence at plan stage; post-merge, the implementation is browser-verified against these criteria. |
| D-05 | **Never name firms.** No page, label, chart, dataset field or blog post names an installer, lessor, PPA provider or financier. Paths use generic labels. Interpretation for other companies: hardware brands are not named in UI copy (the bill of materials lists generic specs, with no store or affiliate links). A dataset publisher (a statistics office, a national lab, a price index, or a retail catalog used as a price sample) MAY be named **only as the cited publisher** on the Sources page, because a citation without a publisher cannot be checked. Company earnings filings are not used as user-facing sources. |
- **R-CONT-01:** the voice is plain, second person and in short sentences (target: a reading grade of ≤ 8 in English). Numbers come before adjectives. No hype, no fear, no sales language (AGENTS.md).
- **R-CONT-02:** the glossary (`jargon-dict.js`, extended) covers every technical term. The visible labels themselves are plain words (F-19). The existing `tests/jargon-lint.test.mjs` is extended to all locales.
- **R-CONT-03:** number display: headlines use 2–3 significant figures; currency has no decimals at or above 100 units; percentages are whole numbers. Full precision appears only in tables and CSV (F-24).
- **R-CONT-04: legal and safety.** `LIABILITY.md` is reflected in concise on-page terms. The DIY path carries the safety block of R-RES-07. The site never suggests unlicensed electrical work.
- **R-CONT-05:** the blog is audited against D-05, the new economics and sources. Stale figures are fixed or removed, and each post shows "last reviewed".
7. **R-RES-07: how to do it.** A country-specific checklist: get two or three quotes, find a licensed electrician, the permit and interconnection steps, the safety rules for DIY mounting (fall protection; the electrician does every electrical termination), and where DIY is not permitted (D-10). No lead forms and no company names.
- **R-SEO-05:** people-first and E-E-A-T signals: methodology, a named maker on `/about/`, sources, dates, a public data changelog and a visible "last reviewed" date on every data page.
Apply R-CONT-01..05 to changed governed content. For blog posts, also verify the P9.7 formatting, SEO, sourcing, and voice criteria; check dated claims against current sources and require a visible review date.

+const INTERNAL_ROOTS = new Set([

+  "docs",
+  "evidence",
+  "jev-artifacts",

+  "D-05",
+  "R-CONT-01",
+  "R-CONT-02",
+  "R-CONT-03",
+  "R-CONT-04",
+  "R-CONT-05",
+  "R-RES-07",
+  "R-SEO-05",

+function git(repoRoot, args) {
+  const result = spawnSync("git", ["-C", repoRoot, ...args], {
+    encoding: "utf8",
+    timeout: 15000,
+    maxBuffer: 8 * 1024 * 1024,
+  });
+  if (result.error)
+    throw new Error(`git ${args[0]} failed: ${result.error.message}`);
+  if (result.status !== 0) {
+    throw new Error(`git ${args[0]} failed: ${(result.stderr || "").trim()}`);
+  }
+  return result.stdout || "";
+}
+
+function requirementLine(planText, id) {
+  const lines = String(planText).split(/\r?\n/);
+  const line = lines.find((candidate) => {
+    const escaped = id.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&");
+    return new RegExp(
+      `^\\s*(?:\\|\\s*${escaped}\\s*\\||-\\s*\\*\\*${escaped}:|\\d+\\.\\s*\\*\\*${escaped}:)`,
+    ).test(candidate);
+  });

+export function extractP97QualityRubric(planText) {

+    requirementLine(planText, id),
+  );
+  return [
+    `Authoritative requirements from ${PLAN_PATH} (read from the candidate; plan hash remains governed by plan:check):`,
+    ...requirements,
+    "Apply R-CONT-01..05 to changed governed content. For blog posts, also verify the P9.7 formatting, SEO, sourcing, and voice criteria; check dated claims against current sources and require a visible review date.",
+  ].join("\n");
+}
+
+export function isGovernedContentPage(file) {
+  const normalized = String(file).replace(/\\/g, "/").replace(/^\.\//, "");
+  if (!/\.html?$/i.test(normalized) || normalized.toLowerCase() === "404.html")

+  const first = normalized.split("/")[0].toLowerCase();
+  return !INTERNAL_ROOTS.has(first) && !first.startsWith(".");
+}

+    /^assets\/data\/.+\.(?:json|csv|xml)$/.test(normalized)
+  );

+export function isGovernedContentFile(file) {

+function parseNameStatus(raw) {
